title: Pocketfold deploy heuristic lane and telemetry ticker — draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, fast-reference playpad for a small-window miniroll ("miniroll") intended for low-risk surface-area changes (config + routing + small model bump). The goal is to pack a cadence anchor, an operations checklist, and a compact telemetry ticker that can be copied into an ops Slack channel or runbook binder.

Scope / When to use:
- Use for changes that need staged traffic but not a full blue/green (e.g., model variant X -> X.q4, routing policy adjustment, batching config tweak).
- Not for schema migrations, infra changes touching DBs, or multi-region DB-backed features.

Quick TL;DR timeline (48h miniroll):
- T-72: Finalize rollout recipe & smoke tests; triage any red tickets.
- T-24: Canary (1%) for 1–2 hours; observe.
- T-12: Gradual ramp to 10% over 30m if green.
- T-6: Hold for internal validation.
- T-0: Ramp to 50% for 1h with close SRE watch.
- T+1h: Full 100% if no regressions.
- T+24h: Post-rollout telemetry digest + retro notes.

Operator checklist (copyable):
- Preflight (T-72 to T-24):
  - Confirm release artifact (sha/tag) in release registry and release-notes entry exists.
  - Verify smoke test harness passes locally and in staging (list: latency smoke, token-budgeting, 95/99 p99 check).
  - Confirm feature flags and kill-switch path in config service (flag id + owner).
  - Ensure canary cohort is defined and health-check endpoints exist.
  - Add watchlist tags in Datadog/Profilius/Tracing for the new release.
  - Notify #release-week and on-call SRE; post initial binder snippet.

- Canary (T-24 -> T-12):
  - Deploy to canary pool (1% traffic).
  - Run synthetic scenarios: short prompt, long-context prompt, streaming path. Capture sample outputs.
  - Watch: 95p latency, p99 latency, error-rate, OOMs, reject-rate.
  - Telemetry quick checks: model-size memory delta, cpu/gpu utilization delta, KV cache hit rate, batch size distribution.
  - If any metric crosses alert thresholds, immediately scale canary down and queue a rollback.

- Ramp (T-12 -> T0):
  - Step to 10% -> 25% -> 50% as described, wait 30m between steps for collection.
  - Verify end-to-end: ingestion -> runtime -> billing counter increments.
  - Confirm cost-per-token sample at each step (sanity check against expected).
  - Run manual queries from Solutions Eng sample prompts; collect outputs and file as artifacts.

- Go/No-go decision ladder (one-line):
  - Green: no new errors, p99 within expected delta, no memory growth, traffic shaping intact -> proceed.
  - Yellow: minor regressions (small latency bump + no error increase) -> hold for 60–120m, enable throttling/shortened contexts if available.
  - Red: error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase OR p99 latency > 2x baseline OR memory growth trending -> rollback to previous artifact.

Telemetry ticker (paste into #release-week during ops):
- Canary metrics snapshot (example):
  - 1% cohort | requests/min: 120 | err_rate: 0.02% | p95: 210ms | p99: 440ms | GPU util: 34% | KV hit: 78%
  - Alerts: none; Observability tags: release:pocketfold-2026-07

- Ramp snapshot template (every step):
  - Traffic % | RPS | err_rate | p95 | p99 | mem_delta | batch_mean | sample_cost
  - Example row: 25% | 3.2k | 0.03% | 220ms | 470ms | +120MB | 8.4 | $0.0012/token

Fallback and rollback play: (short)
- Soft-fail first: scale down new variant -> route 100% back to baseline tag for affected shard.
- If fail persists: full rollback via orchestration (deploy previous image to all pools) and open incident with triage lead.
- Post-rollback: snapshot logs for last 60m, export KV-state delta if possible, tag traces with rollback label.

Smoke-test catalogue (quick):
- Latency smoke: 30 short prompts, median p95 < baseline + 20%
- Regression smoke: 10 golden prompts checked for hallucination/fidelity with the eval harness
- Resource smoke: run steady RPS synthetic for 15m to validate no memory growth > 50MB/min
- Streaming smoke: long-output streaming test for 5 sessions concurrently

Signal thresholds (suggested, tweak per release):
- Error-rate absolute increase > 0.5% -> hard stop
- p99 latency > baseline * 2 -> hard stop
- Sustained GPU OOMs > 1 per 15m -> hard stop
- KV cache hit drop > 15 pts -> investigate (not automatic rollback unless paired with perf regressions)

Comms snippets (copy into Slack):
- Preflight announcement: "Heads up: pocketfold miniroll planned T-24 -> T+24. Canary 1% at T-24. On-call: @SRE-oncall, Release lead: Elliot Rivera. Watch tags: release:pocketfold-2026-07"
- Canary ok: "Canary stable at 1% after 45m. No alerts. Proceeding to 10% at xx:xx UTC unless objections."
- Rollback notice: "Rolling back pocketfold -> baseline (sha: abc123) due to regressing signal(s): [list]. Will update within 20m."

Quick unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Need to confirm whether the billing counter aligns with the new batching profile; Owen to validate runbook for cost-sampling.
- Should we add short-circuit to routing to offload older client versions? Flag gating needs owner.
- Check whether dedicated capacity autoscaler would interfere with a 1% canary on shared pools.

Post-rollout (T+24):
- Pull sample set of 500 requests across cohorts; run automated fidelity eval against golden set.
- Publish a 1-paragraph release note with observed perf deltas, any manual mitigations, and retro action items.
- Fill the release postmortem template if any alerts fired.

Retro prompt (fill after T+24):
- What surprised us?
- Which signals were most useful? Which were noisy?
- What were the blocking tickets and how can we preempt them next time?

References / linked tickets:
- JIRA-RELEASE-312 (rollout recipe)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-engineering/pull/987

Appendix: quick pasteable command snippets (ops):
- Deploy artifact: "rdeploy apply --pool canary --artifact pocketfold:2026-07-18"
- Scale down: "rdeploy scale --pool canary --replicas 0"
- Rollback: "rdeploy rollback --to sha:abc123 --all-pools"

If this doc is useful, we can convert to a 'miniroll template' with automated dashboards (templated Datadog notebook) so ops only paste the cohort snapshots.

End notes: intentionally compact; meant to be pinned to a release binder card and duplicated per-miniroll. Treat the thresholds as suggestions and tune per model family.
